_about: Vocabulary that belongs to some tools only. A match in the build output of a tool not in `owners` fails scripts/build_adapters.py, naming tool/file:line and `why`. `allow` lists `<path>:<line>` places where a match is meant: `<path>` is a suffix of `<tool>/<file in its build>`, so `x/SKILL.md:9` holds in every build and `claude/ONBOARDING.md:7` in Claude Code's alone. An allow that matches nothing fails a full build. Leaks that predate a row are listed in core/terms.baseline, which may only shrink. Patterns are Python regular expressions, case-sensitive unless they start with (?i); `{{commands}}` stands for any ported command's name (PORTED_COMMANDS in the build), so a new command is covered without editing a row. Claude Code's root ONBOARDING.md links every other tool's copy by tool id on line 7, which each tool-name row allows.

rows.why: Claude Code CLI (the kit's own name, claude-starter, is not it)
Claude Code config folder (the kit's clone, ~/.claude-starter, is not it)
Claude Code /clear command (not checked in any other tool)

Claude Code /compact command. OpenCode's onboarding names it, but its TUI docs (opencode.ai/docs/tui, read 2026-11-22) list no /compact, only a session.compact keybind; those two lines are allowed until that is settled
Claude Code tool name (Junie's tool groups share the names)
OpenCode, its CLI or its config folder (~/.config/opencode)
kit command typed after a bare slash (Claude Code namespaces it, Codex types $, the generic build has no command)
kit command as a prompt file
Copilot, its CLI or its config folder
Junie, its CLI or its config folder
ChatGPT plan (Codex runs on one; OpenCode can sign in with one)
AGENTS.md as a rules file: Claude Code ignores it once a CLAUDE.md exists, so it is never Claude's rules target
